notes: National Rail (Darwin/OpenLDBWS) is structurally catalogued here but blocked at the account level — DARWIN_LDB_TOKEN not set. Same blocker as uk-west-midlands / uk-ellesmere-port / east-midlands / south-yorkshire / north-east / west-of-england / south-wales / west-yorkshire.

Single agency (National Rail, operated in-franchise by Transport for Wales), single mode (train), across three geographically independent corridors: North Wales (Wrexham hub), Mid Wales (Aberystwyth terminus, Cambrian Line), West Wales (Carmarthen junction). No second local operator to exclude, unlike South Wales' Valley Lines — see docs/rest-of-wales-d1/jim-handoff.md.

Real-time feed status for Transport for Wales services specifically is UNCONFIRMED (narrower gap than South Wales' 'no feed at all') — static GTFS via Transitland is confirmed live, but whether Darwin/OpenLDBWS actually carries live TfW National Rail data is not established. Treat structurally the same as an unconfirmed feed elsewhere: do not assume it works once DARWIN_LDB_TOKEN is provisioned. See docs/rest-of-wales-d1/jim-handoff.md and hazard-pack.md H2 point 2.

Hub lock: Wrexham General (WRX) only. Aberystwyth (AYW, Mid Wales terminus) and Carmarthen (CMN, West Wales junction) are corridor-significant but explicitly NOT hub-locked — the oracle report gives Wrexham as the clear primary pick and marks the other two lower-priority/secondary.

No inter-corridor through-running within Wales: North Wales <-> Mid Wales routes via Shrewsbury (England, not in catalog); Mid Wales <-> West Wales routes via Swansea/South Wales region (not in catalog). Corridors are operationally independent within this catalog.

Boundary/pass-through stations NOT in this catalog: Chester (CTR, England, North Wales corridor eastbound), Shrewsbury (England, Mid Wales corridor eastbound — no CRS given in the oracle report, none invented here), and the unnamed Carmarthen-to-Swansea continuation (South Wales region boundary, no specific boundary station named in the report).

Four doNotGroup candidates are PROPOSED ONLY, not built: Wrexham General's three route directions, Carmarthen's branch-vs-through-running split, Whitland's three-way branch, Machynlleth's Aberystwyth/Pwllheli split. The oracle report names routes/corridors but gives no platform or service-pattern detail to encode an enforced rule from — confirm against a live Darwin payload once unblocked and TfW real-time status is resolved. See docs/rest-of-wales-d1/hazard-pack.md H4 and doNotGroup proposals.

City id corrected from the D1 pack's 'uk-wales' (which followed a since-fixed stale table in docs/uk-architecture.md) to 'rest-of-wales', matching the established plain-kebab-case convention used by every UK region wired since West Yorkshire (south-wales, west-yorkshire, north-east, etc.) — not uk-south-wales/uk-wales. See docs/rest-of-wales-d1/published-network.json's id-correction note and jim-handoff.md open item 3.

stops.name: Wrexham General
stops.class: hub lock — junction of North Wales Main Line (Chester-Wrexham-Shrewsbury), North Wales Coast Line (Crewe-Wrexham-Holyhead), and Borderlands Line (Wrexham-Bidston/Merseyside); largest North Wales station by connectivity. Not Wrexham Central (southern Borderlands terminus, lower connectivity, never catalogued).

stops.name: Welshpool
stops.class: intermediate, Cambrian Line, Mid Wales corridor

stops.name: Machynlleth
stops.class: junction — Cambrian Line splits toward Aberystwyth or Pwllheli. First in-Wales station east of Shrewsbury (England pass-through, not in catalog). Proposed doNotGroup candidate for the Aberystwyth/Pwllheli split — not built, see notes.

stops.name: Aberystwyth
stops.class: terminus, Mid Wales corridor — secondary hub candidate named in the oracle report but NOT hub-locked (Wrexham General is the sole lock).

stops.name: Pwllheli
stops.class: terminus, Cambrian Line north branch from Machynlleth

stops.name: Carmarthen
stops.class: junction, West Wales corridor — tertiary hub candidate named in the oracle report but NOT hub-locked. Continues east toward Swansea on the South Wales Main Line (South Wales region, not Rest of Wales) — through-running only in that direction, no specific boundary station named in the report. Proposed doNotGroup candidate for the branch-vs-through-running split — not built, see notes.

stops.name: Whitland
stops.class: branch point — Fishguard Harbour / Milford Haven / Pembroke Dock branches split here. Proposed doNotGroup candidate — not built, see notes.

stops.class: terminus, West Wales corridor — DARWIN_LDB_TOKEN not set in this sandbox so FGH (Fishguard Harbour) could not be live-verified per docs/jim-brief-uk-crs-corrections.md; kept FGW and renamed the entry from 'Fishguard Harbour' to its actual station name 'Fishguard & Goodwick' per the brief's fallback instruction.
